jobs.title: Consulting Program Manager, Vice President
jobs.description:
Why this role is important
As part of the consulting function, this role drives execution of large-scale, enterprise-wide strategic programs. This role will support the portfolio manager in effectively managing the portfolio of programs, creating efficiency in execution and building a best in class change consulting function.

Who we are looking for
- As a Consulting Program manager, you will play a critical role in delivering programs required to deliver our strategic priorities.

- This position requires a program manager with a proven track record of owning, driving, and managing successful outcomes associated with complex programs in a dynamic, and time-driven environment that requires risk-based decision-making and effective execution.

- Driven, ambitious individual looking to advance their career in Consulting

Purpose of Role
The Program Manager is responsible for project managing and driving the execution and delivery of change across the Consulting portfolios. This broad portfolio includes strategic, regulatory, business transformation delivering business outcomes across the enterprise.

Key Responsibilities
- Programme Management: Deliver a portfolio of key change initiatives, with front-to-back ownership of the full project lifecycle.

- Stakeholder Engagement: Develop and manage relationships with programme sponsors and partners across business lines and infrastructure, ensuring sustainable and cohesive programme delivery.

- Oversight Framework: Establish and monitor an effective oversight framework to ensure issues and risks are appropriately identified, escalated, and resolved.

- Business Knowledge: Build technical and operational business knowledge to support business understanding and the impact of change management processes on BAU (Business as Usual).

- Communication Strategy: Define a robust communication strategy and provide transparency around delivery progress to all key stakeholders.

- Project Management Tools: Utilize key project management tools and techniques, maintaining document artefacts to a high standard to meet project demands.

- Meeting Leadership: Prepare and lead key project meetings, including steering committees and working groups.

- Team Development: Actively participate in the development and maintenance of the team as a change center of excellence.

What we value
- Experience delivering high-profile complex change programmes in a financial institution

- Strong written and verbal communication

- Objective and results driven

- Very strong attention to detail and accuracy

- Successful track record in problem-solving and successful implementation

- Experience with project management protocols and governance standards

- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications

jobs.title: Program Management Office (PMO) Lead – Alpha Consulting, Vice President
jobs.description:
Who We Are Looking For
Alpha Consulting is seeking an experienced and highly motivated Program Management Office (PMO) Lead to support strategic client transformation programs while helping establish and scale a new consulting PMO capability within Alpha. This leadership role is ideal for an individual who thrives in complex, fast-paced environments and has a proven track record of successfully delivering large-scale business and technology transformation initiatives. The successful candidate will possess strong executive presence, exceptional stakeholder management skills, and the ability to drive accountability and execution across multiple organizations and workstreams.

As a PMO leader, you will play a critical role in shaping delivery standards, driving governance excellence, mentoring project management talent, and helping build a best-in-class consulting organization capable of supporting Alpha's continued growth.

Position Summary
The PMO Lead will be responsible for overseeing the successful delivery of strategic client programs, including the Ariel implementation, while helping build and mature the Alpha Consulting PMO organization.

This individual will serve as the central point of coordination across clients, State Street leadership, implementation teams, product organizations, and operational partners to ensure programs are delivered on time, within scope, and in accordance with established governance standards. The role requires a hands-on leader who can balance executive stakeholder management with strong delivery discipline, ensuring transparency, accountability, and successful outcomes across complex transformation programs. This is a highly visible, client-facing leadership position requiring expertise in program governance, change management, project delivery, organizational leadership, and strategic consulting.

Key Responsibilities
Program Leadership & Delivery
- Serve as the PMO Lead for strategic Alpha client programs, including Ariel and future consulting engagements.
- Provide end-to-end oversight of large-scale transformation programs from mobilization through implementation and stabilization.
- Lead Program Managers, Workstream Project Managers, and PMO resources to ensure successful delivery against milestones, scope, budget, and timelines.
- Develop and manage integrated project plans across business, operational, and technology workstreams.
- Drive resolution of cross-functional risks, issues, dependencies, and delivery challenges.
- Support organizational readiness and transition-to-business-as-usual (BAU) activities.

Governance, Controls & Reporting
- Establish and maintain PMO governance frameworks, delivery methodologies, standards, and best practices.
- Lead steering committees, governance forums, executive reviews, and program status meetings.
- Ensure adherence to Alpha implementation methodology, governance standards, audit requirements, and tollgate processes.
- Own program planning, reporting, and controls utilizing Jira, Confluence, SharePoint, and other project management tools.
- Develop executive dashboards, status reports, RAID logs, action trackers, and key performance metrics.
- Maintain program documentation and evidence repositories to support governance, compliance, and audit requirements.

Executive Stakeholder & Client Management
- Serve as a trusted advisor to client executives and senior State Street leadership.
- Build strong relationships with executive sponsors and key stakeholders across business and technology organizations.
- Facilitate discussions regarding program progress, risks, dependencies, strategic decisions, and overall program health.
- Prepare and present executive-level updates, steering committee materials, and governance reporting.
- Develop communication strategies that promote transparency, accountability, and stakeholder alignment.
- Influence decisions and drive outcomes across organizations without direct reporting authority.

PMO Leadership & Organizational Development
- Help define and execute the vision, operating model, and organizational structure for the Alpha Consulting PMO.
- Establish Alpha Consulting as a center of excellence for program delivery, governance, and change management.
- Develop repeatable delivery frameworks, templates, reporting standards, and best practices.
- Partner with leadership to recruit, mentor, and develop PMO talent.
- Support resource forecasting, capacity planning, budget oversight, and financial management activities.
- Drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance delivery quality, operational efficiency, and client satisfaction.

Qualifications
- 10+ years of Program Management, PMO Leadership, Consulting, or Transformation Management experience.
- Proven track record leading large-scale business and technology transformation programs within financial services.
- Strong executive presence with experience interacting with C-suite and senior stakeholders.
- Expertise in program governance, risk management, project controls, and delivery oversight.
- Experience managing multiple project managers, workstreams, and cross-functional teams.
- Strong stakeholder management, negotiation, communication, and influencing skills.
- Demonstrated ability to operate effectively in fast-paced, deadline-driven environments and drive results through others.
- Advanced knowledge of Jira, Confluence, SharePoint, Microsoft Office, and project reporting tools.
- PMP, PgMP, Agile, or equivalent certification preferred.
- Experience within asset management, investment operations, custody, middle office, Alpha implementations, or platform transformation programs is highly desirable.
- Experience building or scaling PMO organizations, consulting teams, or delivery centers of excellence is a plus.

jobs.title: Corporate Strategy, Managing Director
jobs.description:
Who We Are Looking For
We are seeking an experienced strategy leader to join State Street’s Corporate Strategy team as a Managing Director. Reporting to the SVP, Head of Corporate Strategy, this individual will serve as a senior thought partner to the SVP, supporting the development of enterprise strategy, leading multiple high-priority strategic efforts, and advising senior executives on the firm’s most consequential choices.

The role offers significant exposure to State Street’s Executive Committee and senior leadership, broad influence across the enterprise, and a strong platform for future leadership opportunities. The Corporate Strategy team has a proven record of developing talent for senior roles across the firm.

Why This Role Is Important to Us
The Corporate Strategy team supports the development of the firm’s strategic direction, translates external and internal insights into enterprise choices, and helps senior leaders align resources and execution against the highest-value opportunities. As a Managing Director, you will lead major strategic initiatives, bring an enterprise perspective to complex decisions, translate strategic work into clear actions and outcomes, and strengthen the team’s capabilities.

What You Will Be Responsible For
Strategic Leadership & Execution
- Lead high-priority strategic initiatives from problem definition through recommendation and execution planning
- Frame ambiguous enterprise questions, develop hypotheses, direct analysis, and ensure recommendations are fact-based, practical, and decision-ready
- Support and lead defined components of the firm-wide strategic planning process, translating enterprise direction into clear choices, priorities, resource implications, and measures of success
- Integrate business and functional perspectives while maintaining a firm-wide view of where and how State Street should compete and win
- Monitor market, competitive, client, and execution developments – identifying implications for the strategy and initiating focused analysis when conditions change
- Maintain accountability for the quality, pace, and impact of multiple projects, anticipating risks and intervening to keep work on track

Executive Stakeholder Engagement
- Build trusted relationships with Executive Committee members and other senior leaders, engaging beyond immediate projects to inform the broader strategic agenda
- Facilitate executive-level problem solving, challenge assumptions constructively, and build alignment around difficult choices
- Translate complex analysis into clear, concise narratives and recommendations tailored to executive and Board audiences
- Represent the Corporate Strategy team in senior forums and advance work consistent with the SVP’s direction, as needed

Team Coaching & Culture
- Set clear direction across projects, delegate work in line with team members’ capabilities and development goals, and hold teams accountable for outcomes
- Coordinate staffing and priorities across the project portfolio, balancing enterprise needs, delivery demands, and team capacity
- Coach and develop team members through frequent, specific feedback and meaningful stretch opportunities
- Support career planning and advancement, building a strong pipeline of strategic talent and future firm leaders
- Cultivate an inclusive, collaborative, intellectually rigorous, and high-performance team culture

What We Value
- Enterprise perspective and sound judgment, with the ability to connect market, client, competitive, financial, operational, and organizational considerations
- Exceptional problem structuring, analytical rigor, synthesis, and recommendation development in ambiguous situations
- Executive presence and credibility, with a demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders and mobilize cross-functional teams without relying on formal authority
- Ability to translate complex issues into concise, compelling narratives for executive and Board audiences
- Strong portfolio and project leadership, including prioritization, delegation, quality control, risk management, and accountability across multiple efforts
- Track record of introducing differentiated perspectives and converting strategic insight into actionable outcomes
- Commitment to talent development, inclusive leadership, collaboration, and the success of the broader team
- High integrity, intellectual curiosity, resilience, and agility in a dynamic environment

Education & Preferred Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree required; MBA or equivalent advanced degree preferred
- 15+ years of relevant experience in corporate strategy, strategy consulting, or a related field, including significant leadership responsibility
- Demonstrated experience shaping enterprise strategy and leading multiple complex, cross-functional initiatives from diagnosis through executive decision and execution planning
- Deep understanding of financial services strongly preferred, particularly asset servicing, asset management, markets, wealth, digital assets, or data and analytics
- Proven experience advising senior executives, developing executive- and Board-level materials, and influencing decisions across organizational boundaries
- Demonstrated success leading, coaching, and developing high-performing teams

jobs.title: AI Strategy, Assistant Vice President
jobs.description:
Who We Are Looking For
State Street is seeking a highly motivated and strategic professional to join the AI Strategy & Product Management team as an Officer. Reporting to the AI Strategy & Product Manager, Vice President, this individual will play a key role in helping accelerate the adoption and scaling of Artificial Intelligence capabilities across the organization.
The successful candidate will possess strong analytical, relationship management, and organizational skills, with the ability to navigate complex business environments and coordinate across business, data, product, and technology stakeholders. This role offers a unique opportunity to contribute to the firm's AI strategy, support strategic initiatives, and help drive meaningful business outcomes through AI enablement.

Why This Role Is Important to Us
Artificial Intelligence represents a strategic priority for State Street as we continue to transform how we operate, serve our clients, and generate value across the enterprise. The AI Strategy & Product Management team is responsible for helping define the vision, governance, prioritization, and execution of AI initiatives across businesses and functions.
As an Officer on the team, you will help bridge business objectives and technical execution, enable the successful delivery of AI opportunities while supporting strategic communications, stakeholder engagement, and platform evolution. You will gain broad exposure across the organization while helping shape the future of AI at State Street.

- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to identify opportunities to improve AI adoption, scalability, and business impact.

Required Skills and Experience

- Excellent relationship management and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to build partnerships across diverse teams.
- Strong organizational skills with demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.
- High-level understanding of enterprise data assets, data management concepts, and AI deployment models.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience developing executive-level presentations and reports.
- Analytical mindset with the ability to structure problems and develop practical recommendations.
- Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly PowerPoint and Excel.

Preferred Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in Business, Technology, Data Science, Engineering, Finance, or a related field.
- Experience supporting strategy, product management, transformation, innovation, technology, or AI-related initiatives.
- Exposure to financial services, asset management, asset servicing, or fintech environments.

jobs.title: Corporate Strategy, VP
jobs.description:
Who we are looking for
We are seeking a highly motivated, intellectually curious Vice President to join the Corporate Strategy team. The Vice President will manage complex strategy projects from problem definition through recommendation and execution planning, working closely with senior leaders across the organization. Strong candidates for this role will have demonstrated the ability to structure ambiguous problems, develop fact-based insights, and translate analysis into actionable recommendations. Typical projects could include enterprise and business strategy development, market and competitive intelligence, client segmentation and market sizing, strategic partnerships and acquisitions, market entry or exit, product and client positioning, profitability, and investment prioritization.

Why this role is important to us
The Corporate Strategy team plays a central role in shaping State Street’s future and translating enterprise priorities into strategic choices and action. Across the globe, institutional investors rely on State Street to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. The team sets the firm-wide strategic direction, evaluates the organization’s most consequential strategic questions, and provides objective, data-driven insight across State Street’s businesses to support decisions by senior management and the Board. This is a great opportunity to join a small, high-impact team with direct exposure to State Street’s senior management and Executive Committee. The group has a strong track record of developing talent that advances into leadership roles across the firm.

Join us if making your mark in the financial services industry from day one is a challenge you are up for.

jobs.title: Business Strategy and Planning, AVP
jobs.description:
Who We Are Looking For

State Street PriceStats—the global leader in daily inflation analytics, drawing on millions of online prices and trusted by investors, economists, and central banks—is seeking a Poland-based AVP, Senior Data Enrichment and Economic Analyst. This senior role brings together economic analysis, web-sourced data enrichment, quality oversight for inflation and FX data, product development, and team leadership. The successful candidate will manage work across the data lifecycle, translate complex datasets into market insights at the intersection of inflation and FX, and partner with global Macro Research, Economics, Product, and Technology teams to deliver scalable solutions. The role requires strong analytical judgment, technical capability, attention to detail, and initiative.
Why This Role Is Important to Us
The Poland-based Data Enrichment and Analytics team is part of State Street Data Intelligence (SSDI), which turns differentiated data into actionable investment insights. SSDI offerings include the State Street PriceStats Indices, used by institutional investors and central banks, and the State Street Private Capital Indices, which support private equity and private credit portfolio construction and benchmarking. This role connects the team with Boston-based Economics, Product, and Technology partners, bringing together data enrichment, quantitative analysis, operational controls, and product development as SSDI expands its coverage and capabilities.
Join us if you are passionate about using data, economic insight, and technology to shape the future of investment intelligence.

What You Will Be Responsible For
- Lead the enrichment and classification of economics-focused datasets using statistical methods, business rules, and AI techniques, including evaluating websites across global markets as potential data sources.
- Own local oversight of daily index monitoring, data-quality controls, exception management, and publication readiness for inflation and FX datasets. Address issues and anomalies affecting economic or market interpretation.
- Analyze inflation and FX trends across countries and sectors to identify data requirements, market implications, and product opportunities.
- Drive the development of purchasing power parity (PPP) products with the Boston-based Economics team, drawing on item-level pricing data and a strong understanding of FX and inflation dynamics.
- Lead opportunities to automate manual processes, strengthen controls, and improve end-to-end workflow efficiency, transparency, and resilience.
- Communicate complex technical and macro concepts clearly to internal stakeholders and, where appropriate, clients.
- Oversee and support junior team members by allocating work, setting priorities, reviewing output, providing coaching and feedback, and promoting consistent quality standards.
- Manage multiple workstreams and stakeholder relationships, ensuring risks, dependencies, and timelines are understood and addressed.

What We Value
- Strong knowledge of economic and statistical concepts is essential, with particular expertise at the intersection of inflation and FX—including exchange-rate movements, relative price levels, pass-through to consumer prices, and purchasing power parity—and the ability to translate these relationships into practical market and product insights.
- Experience with structured, unstructured, and web-scraped data, including classification, enrichment, validation, and quality assessment for inflation and FX datasets.
- A proactive, collaborative mindset and a willingness to take ownership of assignments from problem definition through delivery.
- Clear and precise communication, including the ability to tailor technical content for different audiences.
- Ability to guide, coach, and support junior team members while fostering a collaborative working environment.
- Ability to manage priorities and deliver high-quality work within agreed timelines.

Education and Preferred Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in economics, finance, statistics, mathematics, computer science, data science, or a related quantitative field;
- Relevant experience curating and enriching data for inflation and FX analytics, including monitoring price-data quality across multiple country sources and managing exceptions.
- Experience evaluating web-based and other external data sources for relevance, coverage, accessibility, reliability, and continuity.
- Experience training and supporting others on inflation and FX data processes, methodologies, and quality standards is preferred.
- Exposure to data pipelines, automated quality controls, classification models, or AI and machine learning techniques is beneficial.
- Experience with Python, SQL, STATA, MATLAB, or similar analytical tools is helpful.
- Good communication and English language skills (both written and verbal)

Work Requirements: Working hours between 9am-5pm
Location Krakow, Poland (BIG, Zielinskiego Street)

Note: The role requires a minimum of three days per week working form the office

jobs.description:
The State Street Investment Management (SSIM) Chief Operating Officer (COO) is seeking a Global Head of Business Operations (GHBO) to serve as a strategic partner and advisor and lead the integrated management of the Office of the COO. Reporting directly to the COO, the GHBO will coordinate business management, strategic execution, Finance Technology and organizational transformation across the global COO organization.

The GHBO will provide enterprise-wide leadership across business management, portfolio and program governance, financial planning, vendor and third-party oversight, market data, Finance Technology, communications and the Office of the COO. The role will establish the operating cadence, governance, management information and cross-functional coordination needed to translate strategy into measurable business outcomes. Working across Investments, Institutional, Cash, Global Client Coverage Group, the Chief Business Office, Finance, Technology, Data, Marketing and corporate functions, the GHBO will lead a globally distributed organization and influence senior stakeholders across multiple regions.

The successful candidate will combine strategic judgment, financial and technology acumen, disciplined execution and strong people leadership, with the adaptability and integrity required to operate effectively in a complex global environment.

Responsibilities

Business Management of the COO Organization
- Partners with the COO to set strategic and operational objectives aligned with SSIM priorities, ensuring the COO organization meets or exceeds financial and performance benchmarks and key performance indicators. Tracks performance, identifies variances, issues and dependencies, and works with the COO leadership team to develop and execute corrective actions and delivery plans.

- Builds strong relationships across the COO executive leadership team and the broader organization to advance strategic initiatives.

- Partners with the COO leadership team to identify and implement process improvements and organizational optimization opportunities .

- Drives the development and production of productivity and efficiency metrics , business scorecards and executive reporting in partnership with COO leadership .

- Leads the COO quarterly business review process in partnership with COO leadership and business unit teams, ensuring timely completion of agreed actions .

- Serves as a key member of the COO leadership team; helps shape meeting agendas, coordinates follow-up with stakeholders and ensures effective information flow across the leadership team. Represents the COO on relevant IM regional and global operating committees , as appropriate .

- Partners closely with the COO’s Executive Assistant to ensure meetings are scheduled , follow- up actions are completed and ad hoc requests are addressed in a timely manner .

Strategic Initiatives
- Coordinates and manages projects , initiatives and commitments tied directly to the COO’s key priorities.  In partnership with the COO leadership team, maintains an inventory of critical - path initiatives, provides visibility into progress and risks, and promotes alignment across Investments , Global Client Coverage Group , the Chief Business Office and corporate functions so the COO can remain focused on the highest-priority matters .

- Partners closely with the SSIM Chief Administrative Officer’s Office to execute the CEO’s high - priority and critical initiatives in support of annual business goals.
- Co-leads with Finance, in partnership with the COO leadership team, the annual COO strategic investment prioritization process aligned with the budget process. Identifies issues, dependencies and resource constraints that could affect successful execution of strategic priorities; escalates matters requiring COO attention and presents solutions to address root causes and maintain delivery momentum.
- Leads confidential, time-sensitive and other special projects assigned by the COO , delivering high-quality results with minimal direction and limited outside support .

- Partners with the Transformation team on SSIM and COO initiatives that drive operational efficiency and improve the client and employee experience.

Annual Budget and Strategic Plan
- Partners with the CEO’s Office and SSIM Finance on the annual budget and mid-year forecast in close coordination with the COO leadership team.  Manages routine budget requests and issues , develops operating metrics and dashboards , and establishes regular operational reviews with key stakeholders.

- Partners with Corporate Strategy, the COO leadership team and SSIM Finance on strategic plan development and off-cycle adjustments.

Finance Technology Leadership and Ownership

- Owns relationships with strategic technology vendors and service providers supporting finance capabilities, including service performance, commercial management, roadmap alignment and value realization.

- Serves as the senior technology partner to the IM Finance leadership team, providing transparent portfolio reporting, decision support and proactive escalation of delivery issues, dependencies and trade-offs.

Communications and Employee Engagement
- Defines and executes the COO communications strategy , partnering with the leadership team to articulate a compelling vision , strengthen employee engagement and reinforce key messages through senior leaders .

- Coordinates and develops executive materials for presentations, town halls , client meetings , industry engagements and other strategic forums .

- Partners with the COO leadership team and HR to develop and execute employee engagement action plans.

- Partners with the COO leadership team to lead change management and organizational transformation efforts .

Skills and Qualifications
- Strategic, financial and commercial acumen, with the ability to translate enterprise priorities into clear operating plans, investment decisions and measurable outcomes.

- Demonstrated executive leadership in a complex global organization, including responsibility for multidisciplinary teams, operating performance and a portfolio of strategic initiatives.

- Strong knowledge of investment management and the financial, operational, data and technology capabilities that support the business and its funds.

- Proven ability to lead Finance Technology teams and complex multi-year portfolios, including strategy, architecture, prioritization, delivery governance, financial management, vendor oversight and benefits realization.

jobs.title: Program Manager – Client Pathways Transformation, VP III -  State Street Investment Management
jobs.description:
Position Summary
State Street Investment Management (IM), formerly known as State Street Global Advisors (SSGA), is undertaking a multi-year transformation program to modernize its front, middle and back-office capabilities. This initiative is core to IM’s long-term strategy to increase operating leverage, improve scalability, and enhance service delivery for our investment teams.

We are seeking a Vice President, Program Manager to play a central role in driving this complex program forward. Reporting to the MD leading the initiative, this individual will help coordinate execution, engage with business and technology partners, and ensure outcomes are delivered in line with IM’s strategic objectives. The VP will act as a key connector across internal teams and State Street affiliates (Global Delivery, Global Technology Services, and Client Pathways), ensuring transparency, alignment, and accountability across all phases of the program.

This position sits within the Chief Operating Officer (COO) organization at IM and offers the opportunity to shape the future-state operating model for one of the world’s leading investment managers.

Candidate Profile
- Execution-Focused: Operates with a bias towards action in a complex environment while keeping broader strategic goals in view
- Collaborative Leader: Builds trust and drives alignment across business, technology, and partner teams
- Structured Communicator: Able to synthesize information and clearly communicate at multiple levels
- Strategic Thinker: Comfortable working across ambiguity while maintaining focus on enterprise value creation
- Risk- and Control-Minded: Strong understanding of how to integrate risk frameworks into transformation programs
- Detail-Oriented & Disciplined: Brings rigor and structure to financial, operational, and programmatic tracking

Key Responsibilities

Program Execution & Governance
- Drive the day-to-day execution of the Client Pathways transformation program roadmap, ensuring timely delivery of key milestones and outcomes.
- Partner with the SVP to run program governance, including creation of steering committee materials, executive dashboards, facilitation of program/workstream meetings, and coordination of senior leadership updates.
- Track progress and interdependencies across workstreams and proactively identify risks, blockers, or resource gaps.
- Ensure alignment across Technology, Investments, Middle office operations, Risk, Compliance, and Corporate teams.
- Co-lead overall program with the named Alpha Pathways lead, including workstream management, implementation strategy, execution, status and executive reporting, and issue management & escalation.
- Participate in business analysis as needed to understand the full complete ecosystem of enterprise Investment Book of Record (IBOR) and Accounting Book of Record (ABOR) systems, ensuring that the integration meets the specific needs and requirements of State Street IM team for comprehensive portfolio management, reconciliation, and near real-time reporting.
-

Stakeholder Management & Communication
- Act as a liaison between IM and State Street affiliate teams (Global Delivery, Client Pathways, and GTS), supporting alignment on future-state service design and delivery expectations.
- Build and maintain strong relationships across technology, operations, and functional leadership teams.
- Coordinate with Investments and COO leadership to ensure cross-functional needs are incorporated and addressed.
- Understand and drive clarity or priorities on the overall product and technology roadmap, ensuring alignment and clear communication

Operating Model & Service Oversight
- Contribute to the development and implementation of the future-state operating model for outsourced front, middle and back-office services.
- Coordinate with colleagues to incorporate roles, processes, controls, and KPIs into existing governance programs
- Participate in vendor oversight processes, including service-level reviews, issue escalation, and performance tracking.

Risk Management & Controls
- Ensure strong risk and control frameworks are embedded into transformed processes and platforms.
- Partner with Risk, Compliance, and Corporate Audit to anticipate regulatory expectations and internal control standards.
- Support proactive identification and mitigation of risks tied to operating model shifts and service delivery transitions.

Financial Planning & Program Reporting
- Coordinate with finance teams to track program budget and funding allocations across multiple State Street organizations.
- Support multi-year planning and scenario modeling to inform investment decisions and sequencing.
- Deliver accurate and transparent reporting on program financials, KPIs, and program health.
- Management and tracking of program resource costs and associated accounting treatment

Strategic Initiative Integration
- Assist in sequencing broader strategic initiatives (e.g., data enablement, platform enhancements, organizational design) alongside the core transformation roadmap.
- Work closely with the COO Business Operations and CAO teams to align priorities and execution timelines.
- Ensure that critical business capabilities (multi-asset, alternatives, global operations) are considered in design decisions.

Qualifications
- 10 years of experience in financial services, with at least 8 years in program or transformation leadership roles within financial services
- Deep understanding of investment management operations and the front-to-back investment lifecycle of ABOR, IBOR and transaction management systems.
- Strong knowledge of risk and control frameworks, service-level oversight, and operational resiliency practices
- Demonstrated ability to drive complex, cross-functional programs with measurable business outcomes
- Experience working in matrixed, global organizations across multiple stakeholder groups
- Bachelor's degree required.
- Strong proficiency and experience in the Large, Enterprise Technology Program Management
- Strong communication and influencing skills

About State Street Investment Management

What We Do. As the asset management arm of State Street Corporation, State Street Investment Management has served the world’s governments, institutions and financial advisors for over four decades. With a rigorous, risk-aware approach built on research, analysis and market-tested experience, we build from a breadth of active and index strategies to create cost-effective solutions. As stewards, we help portfolio companies see that what is fair for people and sustainable for the planet can deliver long-term performance. And, as pioneers in index, ETF, and ESG investing, we are always inventing new ways to invest. As a result, we have become one of the world’s largest asset managers with trillions of dollars under our care.

We are driven by a desire to help our clients, and those who rely on them, achieve a better future. Work, Live and Grow. We make all efforts to create a great work environment. Our benefits packages are competitive and comprehensive. Details vary by location, but you may expect generous medical care, insurance and savings plans, among other perks. You’ll have access to Flexible Work Programs to help you match your needs. And our wealth of development programs and educational support will help you reach your full potential.

Inclusion, Diversity and Social Responsibility. We truly believe our employees’ diverse backgrounds, experiences and perspectives are a powerful contributor to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive and reach their maximum potential while adding value to both our organization and our clients. We warmly welcome candidates of diverse origin, background, ability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity and personality. Another fundamental value at State Street is active engagement with our communities around the world, both as a partner and a leader. This is not a traditional infrastructure operations leadership role. Instead, the AWS Federated Platform Operations Lead will drive the next generation of cloud operations by leveraging AI, agentic workflows, automation, operational intelligence, reliability engineering, and platform-based support models to improve service quality, reduce operational risk, and accelerate innovation.
The role serves as a key member of the AWS Federated leadership team and will play a pivotal role in shaping the future multi-cloud operating model across State Street.

jobs.title: IAM Engineering & Operations Lead, VP
jobs.description:
Who we are looking for.

State Street Alpha is seeking an experienced Identity & Access Management (IAM) Engineering and Operations Lead to advance IAM operations for Charles River Development SaaS environments. The role combines hands-on engineering, global operational leadership, access governance, privileged access management, automation, service-account security, audit readiness, and continuous improvement across Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, SailPoint, CyberArk, and related identity platforms.

The ideal candidate is a technically credible IAM leader who can direct engineers, resolve complex production access issues, translate enterprise standards into reliable operating practices, and modernize high-volume identity services through automation and measurable controls. The successful candidate will work closely with cybersecurity, infrastructure, cloud engineering, product, operations, risk, compliance, audit, client-facing teams, and enterprise IAM partners.

Why is this role important to us.

The team you will join is part of Charles River Development (CRD), which became part of State Street in 2018. CRD creates enterprise investment management software solutions for large institutions in institutional investment, wealth management, and hedge funds. Together we have created the first open front-to-back platform, State Street Alpha, launched in 2019.

Identity services are foundational to the secure and resilient operation of client-facing SaaS environments. This role is accountable for dependable access administration, least-privilege enforcement, privileged-access controls, identity lifecycle operations, evidence-ready controls, and the transformation of legacy account and group-management practices. The role will also help reduce operational risk by expanding automation, improving service-account hygiene, strengthening segregation of duties, and moving suitable workloads toward passwordless authentication.

What you will be responsible for

IAM Operations Leadership and Service Delivery

- Lead and mentor a global team of IAM engineers and administrators delivering identity operations, access administration, directory services, privileged access, and production support.

- Own operational performance for IAM services, including service health, ticket queues, escalations, incident response, problem management, change execution, runbooks, and stakeholder communications.

- Provide Level 3 technical leadership for complex authentication, authorization, directory, provisioning, and access issues affecting internal teams and client environments.

- Set clear priorities, delivery plans, support coverage, quality expectations, and operational metrics; drive timely resolution while protecting security and control requirements.

- Coordinate recurring working sessions with operational partners to resolve cross-team dependencies and improve end-to-end access request fulfillment.

Directory Services, Entra ID, and Access Administration

- Engineer, administer, and support enterprise Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID environments, including users, groups, organizational units, Group Policy, directory synchronization, connected organizations, and privileged roles.

- Lead joiner, mover, and leaver processes and ensure access is provisioned, changed, disabled, or removed through approved workflows and within required service levels.

- Design and maintain role-based access control models, group structures, entitlement mappings, and least-privilege patterns for SaaS operational and client-support use cases.

- Perform and oversee access fulfillment through SailPoint and approved ticketing workflows, including remediation of failed or manually fulfilled provisioning activities.

- Partner with infrastructure and application teams on directory integrations, authentication patterns, domain migrations, and identity-related production changes.

Privileged Access and Segregation of Duties

- Operate and expand privileged access management using CyberArk, Azure PIM, and approved enterprise controls for administrative, database, RDP, service, and emergency access.

- Ensure privileged access is time-bound where required, supported by approved incident or change records, appropriately authorized, logged, monitored, and periodically reviewed.

- Maintain separation between access administration, approval, system administration, and functional access; identify, escalate, and remediate segregation-of-duty conflicts.

- Coordinate onboarding of privileged accounts, safes, access groups, and client-agnostic operational groups into approved PAM solutions.

- Support break-glass and emergency-access processes, including evidence, review, and post-use validation.

Service Account Governance and Passwordless Modernization

- Lead governance and operational controls for service and other non-human accounts, including inventory, ownership, naming, organizational-unit placement, password age, vaulting, certification, and decommissioning.

- Drive phased migration of suitable service accounts to group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA) or other approved passwordless and key-based authentication patterns.

- Coordinate password-rotation notifications, escalations, change execution, exception handling, and evidence retention for all internal and client owned non-human accounts.

- Partner with SaaS Operations, Product Engineering, Global Operations, and client-facing teams to address dependencies that prevent secure rotation or passwordless conversion.

- Improve monitoring for account changes, stale identities, interactive-logon exposure, and other service-account hygiene risks.

Access Governance, Certifications, and Client Access Controls

- Lead periodic user, privileged, group, guest, and non-human account reviews across CRD SaaS domains and identity platforms.

- Develop scalable methods to analyze direct and nested group membership, cross-domain access, client-domain mismatches, dormant access, and excessive entitlements.

- Ensure remediation from access reviews is completed through approved workflows and that evidence supports internal control, SOC, client, and regulatory requirements.

- Partner with client-facing teams to establish defensible approval patterns for production and non-production access, including start and end dates, business justification, and risk acceptance where required.

- Maintain clear procedures for guest-account inactivity, access recertification, leaver processing, and client identity segregation.

Automation, Engineering, and Continuous Improvement

- Develop and maintain PowerShell and related automation for identity reporting, lifecycle activities, group analysis, access validation, inactive-account controls, and evidence generation.

- Reduce manual effort and operational risk by embedding validation, exception handling, logging, and human approval gates into IAM workflows.

- Use Azure Log Analytics, KQL, Windows security events, and other monitoring capabilities to investigate account activity and support proactive control monitoring.

- Improve IAM architecture and operating practices through maturity assessments, gap analysis, root-cause reviews, roadmap development, and measurable remediation plans.

- Maintain accurate SOPs, procedures, knowledge articles, support documentation, and technical control narratives.

Risk, Audit, Compliance, and Reporting

- Serve as an IAM control owner or delegate for applicable access administration, privileged access, segregation-of-duty, service-account, and identity lifecycle controls.

- Support internal audit, external audit, regulatory examinations, client due diligence, and control testing through complete, accurate, and timely evidence.

- Identify control gaps and operational risks, define sustainable corrective actions, track remediation, and escalate issues through established governance channels.

- Translate enterprise IAM policies and technical standards into actionable CRD operational requirements and implementation plans.

- Provide concise executive reporting on service performance, access risk, control effectiveness, audit commitments, automation progress, and modernization outcomes.

Education & Preferred Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, information systems, cybersecurity, or a related technical field, or equivalent professional experience.

- 10+ years of experience in IAM, directory services, cybersecurity engineering, infrastructure operations, or related technology functions, including experience leading engineers or operational teams.

- Deep hands-on expertise with Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, Windows Server, Group Policy, identity lifecycle management, RBAC, LDAP, DNS, and hybrid identity integration.

- Practical experience with SailPoint or another identity governance and administration platform, and CyberArk or another enterprise privileged access management platform.

jobs.title: Vice President, Data Governance Enablement and Operations
jobs.description:
Why this role is important to us
The Finance organization at State Street plays a critical role in ensuring the accuracy, transparency, and integrity of financial data that informs decision-making across the enterprise. Metadata is the foundation of that transparency – it is what allows us to prove where a number came from, who owns it, how it was transformed, and whether it can be trusted.
This role is responsible for delivering that foundation day to day. As DART matures from a project-based approach to an enterprise capability, the completeness of our metadata and the effective use of our governance tooling determine whether we meet BCBS 239 and regulatory commitments efficiently or through sustained manual effort. This role exists to close that gap through consistent execution.

Role Summary
The VP – Data Governance Enablement and Operations leads the day-to-day delivery of metadata management, data lineage documentation, and data governance tooling operations for Finance, Treasury, and Financial Risk. This role is focused on the operationalization of CDO policies and standards, and business unit priorities.  This role manages the Finance data catalog and CDE inventory and executes the semi-annual CDE metadata and lineage attestation cycle end to end in partnership with other data governance partners.
The role also drives continuous improvement of the governance toolset. The VP identifies automation and efficiency opportunities across Collibra and adjacent platforms, develops business cases and recommendations, and leads delivery of approved enhancements in partnership with the CDO organization, the Data Product and Data Solutions Teams, and Technology.
The VP manages a team of Senior Associate and Officer-level data stewards and governance analysts and serves as the primary working-level contact for metadata and tooling matters with Finance stakeholders and provider teams.

Key Responsibilities
Metadata & Lineage Delivery
- Implement and maintain Finance metadata standards covering business definitions, ownership, classification, lineage requirements, and CDE criteria; recommend updates to senior leadership as requirements evolve.

- Partner with data owners, data stewards, repository teams, and Technology partners to ensure metadata responsibilities are understood and consistently executed.

- Maintain procedure documentation and controls in line with the Global Data Governance Policy, BCBS 239 principles, and regulatory remediation commitments.

- Hands-on expertise in metadata management, data lineage, and CDE frameworks, including practical knowledge of how these artifacts are built, validated, and evidenced.

- Strong working knowledge of enterprise data governance platforms, with direct Collibra experience strongly preferred (catalog, lineage, data quality modules).

jobs.description:
Job Description
State Street Global Treasury Risk Management (GTRM) provides second line oversight of trading market risk across Markets and Treasury divisions as well as liquidity risk, interest rate risk (IRR), investment portfolio mark-to-market risk, and capital risk oversight of the firm’s banking book.

GTRM is a unit within the Financial Risk group of Enterprise Risk Management (ERM). We seek to hire an experienced senior Market Risk Manager to provide second line oversight of capital markets products for both trading and banking book.

Position and Primary Duties and Responsibilities
The Market Risk Manager will:
- Provide expertise on capital markets products, ensuring risk analysis and coverage through new business product approval process

- Perform independent assessments of the overall accuracy, effectiveness, and reliability of the balance sheet interest rate risk management framework

- Provide independent risk oversight of market risk, including identification of risks and drivers, establishment and maintenance of risk limits and other risk controls, measurement and analysis of risks, and monitoring and reporting of risks, including validation of position data and risk calculations

- Participate in special projects and review business strategies and new business initiatives to ensure business objectives are met within the firm’s overall risk appetite.

- Provide review and challenge to first line risk profile and report on changes timely and accurately.

- Support the development of policies, guidelines and operating procedures, according to regulatory requirements and industry best practices.

- Develop and/or improve risk measurements and methodologies to capture all key risk factors as market condition changes and for new business initiatives.

- Prepare analyses, reports and data for senior management, audit, regulatory communication and exams, and rating agency requests.

- Collaborate with the Modelling and Analytics team in implementation of risk metrics and models

- Support risk and/or regulatory projects and remediation as required; independently driving forward assigned tasks

Qualifications, Skills and Experience
- 7+ years of experience in roles related to trading market risk or asset-liability management with a focus on capital markets or balance sheet / capital management.

- At least undergraduate degree in Finance, Economics, Business or quantitative field (such as mathematics, statistics, computer science, etc.) with a proven affinity to financial services; graduate degree or professional designations such as CFA or FRM are a plus.

- Experience with US and EU regulation on trading and market risk.

- Deep knowledge of financial instruments, balance sheet structure and hedging, fund transfer pricing, and applicable risk measures.

- In-depth understanding of financial statements of financial institutions and impacts from central bank policy changes to financial institutions.

- Good working knowledge of financial products, such as fixed income securities, foreign exchange products, interest rate derivatives, equity and securities lending.

- Strong verbal and written communication skills, with ability to articulate effectively ideas and analysis to senior management.

- Self-starter with critical thinking skills and strong financial acumen, willingness to work in a fast-paced and high-energy level environment, and highly organized to manage competing deadlines.

jobs.description:

jobs.description:
Job Description

What we are looking for
As a leader in investment management technology solutions, Charles River continues to expand its offerings. Reporting to the Global Head of Sales, the Global Head of Sales Engineering will oversee a team of approximately 20 Sales Engineers and Solutions Architects.  The Global Head of Sales Engineering will act as a player-coach during the sales process by engaging with clients and prospects on their business requirements and curating meaningful demonstrations with the team.

Why this job is important to us
The team you will be joining is a part of Charles River Development (CRD), that became a part of State Street in 2018. CRD creates enterprise investment management solutions for large institutions in the areas of institutional investment, wealth management, asset owner and alternative managers. We have created the first open front-to-back platform - State Street Alpha, that was launched in 2019. Join us if delivering next generation software solutions using emerging technologies sounds like a challenge you are up for.

Global Head of Sales Engineering
As the Global Head of Sales Engineering, the ideal candidate will act as both a solutions specialist and a leader/mentor to both the sales engineers and solutions architects on the team.  Understanding the investment management space is critical in this role.  Individuals across the sales organization will look to the Global Head of Sales Engineering for guidance and support during the pre-sales process.  This will involve planning and executing complex product demonstrations and proof of concepts by including the most suited members of the team as well as engaging with product management and implementation to align on messaging and orchestrating smooth transitions across the lifecycle of the engagement.

Responsibilities:
- Lead and develop the sales engineering and solution architect groups through regular coaching, individual touch points, and hands on training

- Manage complex resource requirements for new client engagements (ability to balance the appropriate mix of individuals to support the success of the project).

- Must be able to act as a presenter for team members.  Will require full knowledge of the platform solution and strong communication skills to sophisticated investment managers.

- Gather client requirements and work with team to develop meaningful sales demonstrations.

- Act as a platform solutions specialist during the sales process

- Interact with clients: presenting new features, gathering feedback.

- Understand upcoming product release features and be able to demonstrate these updates to the team for consistency.

- Serve as a bridge to the implementation team by effectively communicating and documenting requirements from the pre-sales process.

- Travel requirement: 50%

What you are responsible for
- Lead and mentor the Sales Engineering and Solutions Architect team

- Working in a dynamic, fast-paced environment, apply expertise in specific product areas to deliver a high-quality product

- Partner with Sales leaders and teams to support the sales process through understanding of customer requirements, and demonstrating the value of how our platform solves complex use cases.

- Interact with clients: presenting new features, gathering feedback.

- Work with the product management team in understanding the market needs and developing targeted workflows for client demonstrations.

- Create and maintain a library of standardized demos

- Review all outbound RFP/RFI responses to insure the best solution is being presented to prospects

What we value
These skills will help you succeed in this role:
- Proven ability to manage a large and diverse team of experienced professionals.

- Proven ability to successfully lead teams and functions with a track record of setting realistic yet challenging goals. Instills a strong sense of purpose while also developing a highly engaged team.

- Ability to develop and deliver complex commercial software to demanding clients.

- Strong ability to drive results and execute amid ambiguity. The ability to innovate and problem solve is critical.

- Communicates, collaborates, and influences effectively with internal groups and external clients.

- Can articulate the product vision, roadmap, and capabilities in a clear, concise, and compelling way.

- Engages and energizes the teams across the organization to drive towards successfully meeting client and market needs (product management, engineering, implementation and sales).

Education and Preferred Qualifications

- Advanced degree in mathematical finance, engineering, or business preferred.

- Deep knowledge of financial markets and buyside investment processes.

- Minimum of 15 years of experience in a similar role within Investment Management (Sales Engineering or similar role).

- Minimum of 5 years in a leadership role, preferably in a pre-sales capacity.

- Good understanding of financial investment products across asset classes including derivatives.  Experience with Charles River IMS or similar investment management platform preferred.

- Understanding of buy-side investment management workflows highly desirable

- Excellent communication skills (verbal and written), good interpersonal skills, ability to gather and understand requirements in the financial sector

- Proven organizational skills with attention to detail

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

- Flexibility with schedule and ability to work beyond regular business hours

- Demonstrated planning and scheduling skills

- Ability to work on multiple initiatives simultaneously and deal with the inevitable surprises that are part of a dynamic environment

jobs.title: Business Development & Partnerships, Charles River Development, Assistant Vice President
jobs.description:
Why this role is important to us
You will be joining the Business Development team in Charles River Development (CRD).  The mission of the team is to manage existing partners across the full spectrum of the CRD business, including but not limited to, Trading Partners such as Sell Sides, Trading Venues, and Data providers.  The team also coordinates across functions to drive the creation of new partnerships that add new capabilities to the CRD platform, address customer feedback, and ultimately drive revenue.

Core Responsibilities
New Partnerships - Manage the Business Development Lifecycle
- Work with prospective FIX Counterparts to expand liquidity options and price discovery for CRD Clients.
- Interface with R&D, Product Strategy, and Sales to identify functional areas where new partnerships are needed.
- Collaborate with Product Management to evaluate potential partners, including their functionality, integration capabilities, and pricing.
- Drive the commercial negotiation that results in the basic terms of the partnership.
- Work with Legal and Procurement teams to create a contract that will govern the partnership.
- Following execution of the partnership, work with Sales Enablement and Marketing to establish a Go-To-Market plan.

Existing Partnerships
- You will manage a set of partners. - Maintain strategic relationships with top producing brokers, including leveraging knowledge of their trading workflows and mutual customers.
- Build relationships with the 500+ Sell Sides on the Charles River FIX Network globally.
- Maintain monthly reporting, billing and risk inquiries, and more.
- Manage contract renewals, amendments, and assignments as needed.

- Manage the relationship with the partner, including solving problems in the partnership and working together to drive revenue for CRD and the partner.
- Become knowledgeable of the partner offering and the commercial aspects of the partnership.
- Liaise with internal stakeholders about the partner and collaborate with partners when necessary.
- Become familiar with the commercial arrangement of the partners that you manage.
- Partner with other departments across the organization to support partner engagement, including but not limited to Product, Sales, Client Management, Legal, and Finance/Accounting.
- Support product management in delivering their medium and long term road map.  Work with Product and Strategy to identify and execute on strategic partnerships to add value to the CRD ecosystem. New market assessment and sizing

Other Responsibilities
- Competitive analysis
- Assess vendor risk.
- Ad hoc reporting
- Strategic Projects
- Drive strategic industry analysis and competitive intelligence.
- Drive positioning and content for products and solutions.
- Work with finance to analyze product profitability and sales success of all offerings.
- Validate new market opportunities for our products and solutions.
- Assess client interest in new relationships and monitor ongoing feedback on existing partnership.
- Maintain prioritized requests from sales and clients.
- Assist Sales/Client Management in client discussions around brokers/venues/workflows.
- Serve as an escalation point for the FIX Network Ops team.

What we value
Required
- Must have a strong understanding of Electronic Trading workflows from both a business and technical perspective across all asset classes. Including but not limited to Trader workflows, Connectivity details, FIX protocol.
- Ability to prioritize
- Proficient in Microsoft PowerPoint and Excel
- Ability to ‘role up sleeves’, solve problems, and climb learning curve
- Project management skills
- Excellent follow-through, attention to detail and time management skills
- Familiarity with the vendor ecosystem in buy side technology used by institutional asset managers, asset owners, hedge funds, etc.
- Strong candidates will have worked in commercial software and taken part in both initial stages of business vetting and final role out of partnerships
- Specific knowledge of the investment industry (financial instruments, workflows, major players, macro-economic influences, trends, etc.)

jobs.title: Technology Cost Transparency & Governance Lead
jobs.description:
Who we   are   looking for
We are looking for a Technology Cost Management subject matter expert, Vice President, reporting to the VP leading product, tooling, and transformation within the Global Technology Services Financial Operations Office. In this role you will build and lead a Technology Financial Management and Total Cost of Ownership capability within the Global Technology Services Financial Operations Office.

Why this role is important to us
This role will lead the business design and governance of State Street’s technology cost management capability, helping Global Technology Services provide clear, consistent insight into technology spend, cost ownership, optimization opportunities, and financial decisions for technology leaders and business stakeholders. The successful candidate will combine finance expertise, technology fluency, and strong partnership to build trusted cost transparency practices that support executive reporting, enterprise accountability, and better business decisions.
This Vice President will own the business methodology for cost management, including cost model design, allocation logic, showback, future chargeback enablement, optimization tracking, and benefit validation. The ideal candidate can turn complex cost and operating data into clear, defensible insights for senior leaders.

Why This Role Is Important to Us
Global Technology Services is expanding how it understands, governs, and manages spend across infrastructure, applications, cloud, labor, and services. This role will define how cost is measured, allocated, reported, and optimized, giving technology leadership, finance, and business stakeholders a consistent, well-governed basis for decisions. It will partner with analytics engineering, Finance, Procurement, platform, and technology owners to ensure the methodology is practical, governed, and fit for enterprise use.

What You Will Be Responsible For
- Own the TCO/ITFM methodology, including cost pools, allocation rules, service and product costing, assumptions, and change history.

- Establish showback reporting and chargeback preparedness, including methodology, policy inputs, stakeholder alignment, and governance.
- Define the framework for identifying, sizing, tracking, and reporting cost optimization opportunities.
- Set logic for validating realized savings against targets, separating deterministic results, estimates, and advisory analysis.
- Define KPIs, reporting standards, and executive narratives that make cost transparency and optimization performance clear to senior leaders.
- Translate financial policy, business needs, and operational realities into requirements for analytics and data delivery partners.
- Validate that implemented calculations and data products reflect the agreed methodology and are suitable for leadership reporting.
- Partner with finance, procurement, infrastructure, application, cloud, service catalog, and configuration management teams to improve source data.
- Maintain documentation, assumptions, decision records, and governed methodology artifacts for consistency, repeatability, and auditability over time.
- Serve as a trusted point of contact for cost questions, aligning technical and non-technical stakeholders on definitions, logic, and results.

What We Value
These skills will help you succeed:
- Strong understanding of ITFM, TCO, cost allocation, showback, chargeback, and cost transparency.
- Ability to connect financial discipline with the operating reality of a large enterprise technology organization.
- Strong analytical judgment, including the ability to distinguish actuals, forecasts, assumptions, estimates, and recommendations.
- Clear communication style for senior leaders, finance partners, technology teams, and non-technical audiences.
- Comfort working across functions, resolving ambiguity, and building alignment where definitions and ownership are still maturing.
- Exacting standards for documentation, governance, consistency, and repeatable decisions.

Education & Preferred Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, Information Systems, Operations Management, or a related field preferred.

- MBA or relevant advanced degree preferred; equivalent experience may be considered.
- Experience in ITFM, TCO, FinOps, finance transformation, business operations, and related fields.
- Experience designing or operating cost allocation, showback, chargeback, unit costing, service costing, or benefit tracking frameworks.
- Experience defining KPIs, allocation methods, and reporting standards for executive financial or operational reporting.
- Experience translating financial and operational requirements into analytics, reporting, or data product requirements.
- Familiarity with TBM taxonomy or comparable cost frameworks.
- Experience with infrastructure, application inventory, cloud, CMDB, service catalog, or product taxonomy data preferred.
- Relevant certifications or training preferred, such as TBM Practitioner, financial analysis, technology, finance, or service management credentials.
- Experience working in financial services or another regulated enterprise environment preferred.

Additional Requirements
The role requires strong partnership across finance, technology, procurement, analytics engineering, and governance stakeholders. The candidate should be comfortable operating in a matrixed environment with evolving requirements, data quality considerations, and leadership reporting needs.

jobs.description:
Who we are looking for:
The Sustainable Investing Research Analyst is a member of the Sustainable Investing Research team within State Street Investment Management’s Sustainable Investing organization. The role is responsible for leading investment-relevant quantitative research projects and the implementation of the team’s capabilities to enable investment teams to meet client objectives. The SI Research Analyst is a key contributor to State Street Investment Management’s industry leading sustainable investing research capability and sustainable investment solution innovation in order to meet rising client demand. The position is based in Boston and reports to the Global Head of Sustainable Investing Research.

Why this role is important to us:
The team you will be joining is a part of State Street Investment Management, one of the largest asset managers in the world. We partner with many of the world’s largest, most sophisticated investors and financial intermediaries to help them reach their goals through a rigorous, research-driven investment process. With over four decades of experience and trillions of dollars in assets under management, we offer one of the broadest selections of products and strategies across asset classes, risk profiles, regions and styles. As pioneers in index, ETF, and sustainable investing, we are always inventing new ways to invest.

The Sustainable Investing Research (“SI Research”) team conducts thematic research, produces thought leadership, enables product innovation, and ensures the integrity of sustainable investing data that is integrated in client portfolios to achieve various sustainable investing objectives. Through its expertise, it enables sustainable investing product development and develops new capabilities to support product innovation, with the goal of ensuring these capabilities are credible in their approach to achieving sustainable investing objectives. As part of its mandate to ensure data integrity, the team owns the firm’s sustainable investing data and vendor strategy to stay on top of emerging capabilities, acts as the center of expertise on sustainable investing data for investment teams, and maintains strong data monitoring and governance practices.

What you will be responsible for:
- Lead quantitative research projects that enable sustainable investing product innovation
- Develop credible implementation methodologies to new investment approaches, e.g., sustainable outcome investing
- Partner with PM teams to conduct asset class-specific research on sustainability factors and to support client solutions
- Oversee the implementation of sustainable investment capabilities in internal systems, including ensuring strong data governance
- Develop thought leadership pieces to demonstrate State Street Investment Management’s sustainable investing capabilities, focusing on financial materiality

Required qualifications and skills:
- 7+ years of experience in quantitative research and data analysis in the asset management industry, preferably with a large global asset manager, asset owner, or investment consulting organization
- Understanding of the investment process and how sustainability factors can be integrated to achieve client objectives
- Strong intellectual curiosity and passion in understanding how sustainability factors drive long-term value, with a practical mindset in applying the research output to create and enhance investment solutions
- Self-starter with ability to set priorities and execute research projects
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain data concepts to non-technical stakeholders

jobs.title: Risk Analyst, Officer, State Street Investment Management
jobs.description:
Who we are looking for

As a Risk Analyst within State Street Investment Management’ Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) team, you will provide an independent investment and liquidity risk oversight across asset classes and products offered by SSIM. You will use your abilities to analyze qualitative and quantitative information and develop and implement plans to mitigate risks to SSIM.
In this role you can anticipate substantive interaction with several global business functions, such as Investment Management, Trading, Product, Legal and Compliance, and will need to communicate effectively with a wide range of people. You will also work closely with our Technology Risk partners to drive improvement in productivity via automation initiatives, to execute our digital transformation strategy. You will drive a risk-aware culture throughout the organization by challenging the status quo and providing objective thought leadership to our organization and the financial industry.

We are looking for an Officer level experience, driven and motivated by financial markets and risk management

Why this role is important to us

State Street Investment Management is one of the largest asset managers on the World with over $6 trillion of Assets Under Management (AUM). It is also the investment management arm of State Street Corporation, one of the world’s leading providers of financial services to institutions. Institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. We keep our clients at the heart of everything we do, and smart, engaged employees are critical to our continued success.
The Global ERM team consists of over 70 risk professionals located in various locations across US, EMEA and APAC. As a combined group, we are responsible for identification, assessment, control and  reporting of risk in four main areas: operational, investment, liquidity, credit, and model risk.

What you will be responsible for

- Perform risk monitoring, analyze risk exceedances and cooperate with the Business/ Portfolio Managers to determine the root causes of threshold breaches and address the associated risks.
- Work together with various teams to execute, expand and improve SSIM’s overall risk management framework.
- Undertake independent research on risk management
- Participate in global ERM projects to enhance our framework and data environment.
- Provide expertise and strong cross-risk discipline insights by serving as a key contact for risk queries and collaborating with other risk and internal control functions.
- Work at the forefront of financial regulatory developments, new products, services and applications as well as assess and report on their respective impacts to the business's risk profile.

What we value

- Financial Services experience a plus

We are currently hiring for a sales distribution role within the Client Coverage Group at State Street Investment Management (SSIM). The Associate Regional Consultant, Model Portfolios – US Wealth, AVP, State Street Investment Managemen will join our U.S. Wealth team and work alongside a team of model distribution professionals to build and deepen relationships with financial advisors across the Broker Dealer channel

The Associate Regional Consultant, Model Portfolios – US Wealth, AVP will be responsible for developing and managing a select group of advisor relationships, with a focus on driving engagement and adoption of our model portfolio offerings. The role will combine digital engagement, including phone and virtual meetings, along with travel across the territory to build relationships and identify sales opportunities.

The successful candidate will serve as a trusted resource to financial advisors, develop a strong understanding of their investment needs, and effectively position our model portfolio capabilities. The position will be a hybrid sales role, with focused travel and time in the office.

- Own and grow a defined subset of financial advisor relationships within the Broker Dealer channel, using a combination of digital engagement and focused territory travel to cultivate relationships and drive adoption of SSIM Model Portfolios
- Identify client needs across a range of business practices and deliver relevant market insights, product information, investment ideas, and sales support on a consistent basis.

State Street seeks to recruit a Head of Technology Governance and Program Management to significantly uplift its independent governance of risk, regulatory program management and remediation while bringing connectivity and consistency of execution through dependency management, transparent reporting and improved overall accountability. This role will be primarily based in US (preferably Boston) and will consider candidates based in London, UK location. Internal associates will be considered for this role.
